note: BUG#22 (QualityControl ledger) — the OTHER half of hydrate_existing's own route-forces-find shape, alongside bug22_route_forces_find_or_notfound_legacy_creates.json's NotFound case: when the route DOES resolve to a genuinely existing record, Ruby's CommandInterpreter#hydrate_existing returns that record and the SAME dispatch (Grant's own mutations) runs against it as an ACT, not a fresh creation — step_assign_creation_attributes is skipped entirely (legacy_implicit_creation? is false whenever a route was given), so a second Grant routed at an already-granted RoleTransition's own identity re-runs Grant's mutations and re-emits RoleTransitionGranted rather than refusing AlreadyExists or minting a duplicate. Unmodified Rust's generated dispatch never modeled this at all — a creates: command's generated fn only ever knew how to build a fresh record (Hydrate::Create), with no code path standing in for Hydrate::Act. Confirmed genuinely broken before this fixture existed (unmodified Rust silently created/overwrote via facts instead).
